evidence: Read CONTEXT whole, then the draft: 'It’s still one grown-up doing three jobs (nobody new is moving in to help with the rent), and each job keeps the others in balance.' It appears once in CONTEXT and is identical to DRAFT.txt, between 'I’m going to talk about it in terms of three jobs: your loving Nurturer, your safe Adult Protector (hereafter just the Protector) and your wise Guide.' and 'Say a party gets to be too much for your little one.' Read in place there is no seam: 'three jobs' in the sentence before is answered by 'still one grown-up', the rent joke still plays on 'three jobs' (several jobs to pay the rent), and the party example that follows still shows the three jobs balancing each other. Against SOURCE ('That’s one grown-up doing three jobs, not three more people moving in to help with the rent, and each job keeps the others in balance.'): the same three parts in the same order (one grown-up; no extra people, his rent joke; 'each job keeps the others in balance', word for word). The only edits are 'That’s' to 'It’s still', 'not three more people moving in' to '(nobody new is moving in)', and the commas to brackets. 'still' carries the concession (three named jobs, still one person) that 'not three more people' carried, and adds no fact. Dropping 'three' from 'three more people' loses nothing because 'three jobs' is in the same sentence. 'It’s' points at the arrangement just described, as 'That’s' did, and a reader does not stumble (C02 ABSENT). Typography matches the surrounding text (curly apostrophe, one space before the bracket, no space before the full stop). A second bracket sits one sentence after '(hereafter just the Protector)', but it is a different kind (a joke aside, against a definition) and brackets are already this paragraph's habit, so I do not count it as a seam. Tell rows: all 33 (T01-T29, C01-C04) checked against the literal draft in context; none is PRESENT. T16 was in the source ('That’s X, not Y') and the change removes the reveal. The contrast that remains (one grown-up, nobody new) answers a real misreading of 'three jobs' as three people, so it is a natural contrast, not the reflex (T12 ABSENT). T18 ABSENT: the line is not a short flip, it also carries the balance claim. T15 ABSENT: the reveal clause becomes a bracketed joke, which changes the shape, not a swap for rarer words. T21 ABSENT: the same parts as his sentence, none added. T26 ABSENT: 'three jobs' repeats the sentence before, and the repetition does the turn from three to one, as in his line. T17 ABSENT: 'each job keeps the others in balance' is his clause, unchanged. T13 and T09: his rent joke is where the sentence puts its weight. No first person, scene, tic word, colon or question, and it is not a paragraph end (T20, T29). Linter finding 'D9 follows the source order' (1/1 paragraphs, agreement 1.00): accepted. The change is a one-sentence in-place edit of his line that keeps its clause order by design, nothing is reordered (T14 ABSENT), and the sentence notices something along the way (the rent joke), which is the flag's own test (T13, T09). I could not check the Pangram readings in the_change (no web); none were needed to judge meaning, voice or tells.
